answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2021, Clause 3.3.2 (Pressure at outlets), the minimum working pressure at the furthermost or most disadvantaged fixture or outlet shall be not less than 50 kPa (5 m head), at the flow rate specified in Table 3.2.1. The library text states: "The minimum working pressure at the furthermost or most disadvantaged fixture or outlet shall be not less than 50 kPa (5 m head), at the flow rate specified in Table 3.2.1." (The excerpt is set with the clause headings interleaved, but the sentence falls under Clause 3.3.2 Pressure at outlets.) NOTE 1 adds that storage tanks to Section 8 or booster pumps to Section 13 may be required to achieve the minimum pressure, and NOTE 2 that some fixtures may require more than 50 kPa. Appendix C, Step 3 confirms: "Clause 3.3.2 requires a minimum value of 5 m head". Edition used: AS/NZS 3500.1:2021 (edition_status: published). This is the edition held in the library; the question asks for the 2021 edition, which matches. Note the house rule: AS/NZS 3500.2's 2025 edition was published 2025-04-17 — that is a different Part (sanitary plumbing and drainage); for Part 1 the library holds the 2021 published edition, and whether a newer Part 1 edition exists should be checked separately.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2021, clause 3.3.4 (Maximum pressure within buildings) states: "The maximum static pressure at any outlet, other than a fire service outlet, within a building shall not exceed 500 kPa." A note adds that pressures above 500 kPa can cause damage from water hammer, reduced life of appliances, taps and fittings, and excessive noise in the system. Note the excerpt heading labels this clause as 3.3.4 in the body text, alongside clause numbering 3.3.1–3.3.5; the value itself is 500 kPa.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2021, a reduced pressure zone device (RPZD) must have its relief drain outlet located not less than 300 mm above the finished surface level. Clause 4.6.3.2(d) states that RPZDs shall — "(i) have free ventilation to the atmosphere for the relief valve outlet, at all times; (ii) not be located in an area that may be subjected to ponding or freezing; (iii) have the relief drain outlet located not less than 300 mm above the finished surface level." The same 300 mm minimum above finished surface level also applies to the reduced pressure detector assembly (RPDA) under 4.6.3.2(f)(iii). Edition used: AS/NZS 3500.1:2021 (published, edition_status: published). This is the edition held in the library; the question specifies the 2021 edition, so no superseded-edition caveat applies to the edition asked about.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2021 Clause 5.3.3.1(a)(i), the minimum separation between an underground water service pipe not greater than DN 65 and an electrical supply cable that is indicated along its length with orange marker tape and mechanically protected is 100 mm. The clause reads: "100 mm for a water service pipe not greater than DN 65, where the electrical supply cable is indicated along its length with orange marker tape and is mechanically protected". (A 300 mm separation applies only where the water service pipe is greater than DN 65, and 600 mm where the cable is neither indicated nor protected.) This is the published AS/NZS 3500.1:2021 edition and is current — it is not superseded; the 2015, 2018 and 2003 excerpts shown are superseded editions but state the same 100 mm figure.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2021, Clause 5.3.3.4 (Stormwater and sanitary drainage), a water service pipe may be laid in the same trench as a drain provided it is located on a shelf or ledge excavated at one side of the trench not less than 50 mm from the continuation of the trench, or on compacted bedding such that the horizontal separation of the two pipes is not less than 100 mm, with the required depth of cover maintained. In addition, the underside of the water pipe must be at least 100 mm above the top of the drain. Therefore, on compacted bedding the minimum horizontal separation is 100 mm.

answers.answer: For a water service pipe greater than DN 65 (DN 80 is greater than DN 65), Clause 5.3.3.6 requires a separation of at least 300 mm from any other service, other than consumer gas piping and electrical or communication services (which have their own rules in 5.3.3.1–5.3.3.3). If the case in question is a crossover (the water service crossing the other service), Clause 5.3.4 sets a vertical separation of not less than 100 mm, crossing at an angle not less than 45°, with marker tape laid 150 mm above the installed service for 1 m either side of the centre-line. So: 300 mm where the DN 80 pipe runs past another service; 100 mm vertical separation at a crossing.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2021, water service pipes laid beneath a concrete slab on ground must have a minimum distance of 75 mm between the top of the pipe and the underside of the slab or slab-stiffening beam. Clause 5.5.4(a) requires the pipes be laid in a narrow trench on a bed of sand or fine-grained soil, placed and compacted so the piping is not damaged, and states: 'There shall be a minimum distance of 75 mm between the top of the pipe and the underside of the slab or slab-stiffening beam.' The 2021 edition is the published (current) edition in the library and is not superseded.

answers.answer: For water service pipes beneath concrete slabs on ground that penetrate the slab, the penetrating pipework must be at right angles to the slab surface and lagged for the full depth of the slab penetration with an impermeable flexible material of not less than 6 mm thickness, or with an impermeable plastics sleeve or conduit providing equivalent protection. Under Clause 5.5.4(c) of AS/NZS 3500.1:2021, the minimum thickness of the impermeable flexible material is therefore 6 mm.

answers.answer: AS/NZS 3500.1:2021, Clause 5.18.2 (Piping located outside buildings), under 5.18.1 General (protection against freezing): in areas where the ambient temperature regularly falls below 0 °C, all pipes and fittings shall be either — (a) buried to a minimum depth of 300 mm, measured from the proposed finished surface level to the top of the pipe; or (b) surrounded with waterproof thermal insulation of a minimum thickness as given in Table 5.18.2(A). So the minimum burial depth for piping outside a building is 300 mm from the proposed finished surface level to the top of the pipe (unless the insulation option in (b) is used).

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2021, a water service pipe running alongside an external wall must be positioned not less than 20 mm away from the external surface of the wall (Clause 5.18.4.3, p.60). The library text states: "Pipes adjacent to external walls shall be positioned not less than 20 mm away from the external surface." A NOTE adds that, where practicable, pipes should be located on the heated side of any wall insulation present. Note the stated context of Clause 5.18 is insulation/freezing protection; the 20 mm clearance is the only minimum given for pipes adjacent to external walls.
values: 20 mm minimum clearance from the external wall surface

answers.answer: Type A irrigation system outlets and piping must be installed more than 150 mm above finished ground level (and clear of surface ponding). Note the library excerpts do not show a numbered clause 7.2.1 or a separate numeric minimum-height clause; the 150 mm figure appears in the Clause 7.2 system-type definition and in Figure 7.2(A).

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2021, the total length of branch connections to fixtures on an unvented branch drain serving ground-floor fixtures must not exceed 10 m. Figure 3.10.3 states: "NOTE Total length of branch connections to fixtures to not exceed 10 m." This is consistent with Clause 3.10.3 (Maximum length), which limits the total length of an unvented branch drain, including the length of the fixture discharge pipe, to not greater than 10 m from the vented drain to the weir of the trap (and 10 m from the weir of a disconnector gully). Note also that individual fixture discharge pipe limits apply (e.g. 2.5 m for basins/bidets with S-traps, 2 m vertical drop for WC pans with DN 80, etc.), but the overall total for branch connections to fixtures is 10 m.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2021 the minimum height of the overflow point below the lowest fixture is 150 mm. Clause 4.6.6.6 states: "A minimum height of 150 mm shall be maintained between the top of the overflow gully riser and the lowest fixture connected to the drain. This height shall be measured vertically from the overflow level of the gully riser or from the invert level of the overflow pipe to the point given in Table 4.6.6.6." The same 150 mm is shown graphically in Figure 4.6.6.5 as "150 min. below lowest fixture" from the invert level. Note: the 150 mm is measured to the point of measurement listed in Table 4.6.6.6 for the fixture in question (e.g. top surface level of the water seal for a soil fixture with integral trap; top surface level of the grate for a floor waste gully or shower). A separate 75 mm minimum applies above the surrounding finished surface level (Clause 4.6.6.7).

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2021, where a domestic bar sink discharges to a floor waste gully and is trapped and connected to the riser of the floor waste gully, the maximum length of the waste pipe is 2.5 m. Table 4.6.7.2 gives, for 'Bar sink (domestic)': untrapped connected to riser = 1.2 m; trapped connected to riser = 2.5 m; and trapped or untrapped to a submerged inlet FWG = 2.5 m. The same limit appears in the commentary to Figure 4.6.7.1 ('Trapped waste 2.5 m long max. Untrapped waste 1.2 m long max.'). Clause 4.6.7.3 also requires each fixture (or fixture pair) connected to an FWG to be connected by a separate waste pipe at a grade of not less than 2.5% and with a length not exceeding that in Table 4.6.7.2. In addition, Clause 13.18.2 requires a domestic bar sink to be connected either by an untrapped waste pipe not smaller than DN 40 to a floor waste gully, or by a trap and waste pipe not smaller than DN 40. Note: the edition used is AS/NZS 3500.2:2021, which is the edition in the excerpt; the library summary in the house rules notes that AS/NZS 3500.2:2025 was published 2025-04-17, so the 2021 edition is superseded — check the 2025 edition for current requirements.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2021, a floor waste gully must have a riser of not less than DN 80 to finished surface level, except where the sole function of the FWG is to dispose of water spillage and wash-down water, in which case a minimum DN 50 riser may be used. Clause 4.6.7.6 ('Removable grate') states: 'Floor waste gullies shall be installed with an accessible removable grate and have a riser of not less than DN 80 to finished surface level. Where the sole function of the FWG is to dispose of water spillage and wash-down water, a minimum DN 50 riser may be used.' Note that a separate provision, Clause 4.6.7.9 ('Size of gully trap outlet'), deals with the outlet size (not the riser) and shares the same exception wording for DN 50 where the sole function is spillage/wash-down water.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2021, Clause 6.6.2.4.2 (New installations), where a junction is used to make the connection of a DN 100 branch pipe to another DN 100 pipe, the entry level of the branch pipe shall be elevated at an incline of not less than 15° above the horizontal. The clause's NOTE 2 explains that positioning the junction a minimum of 15° above horizontal removes the probability of partial backwash of a discharge into the branch causing stranding that can lead to blockages. Note: this is the sanitary plumbing/drainage (discharge pipe) requirement; the parallel drain provision in Clause 4.9.1.2 uses the same 15° figure for a DN 100 branch drain.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2021, Clause 6.7.1 covers 'Types' of junctions in stacks and does not itself contain the 500 mm restriction. answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2021 Clause 6.8.3(b), where a stack connects to a graded pipe or drain above ground using a 45° junction installed in the vertical plane with an extended branch, the extended branch must be arranged "so that the vertical projection of the stack, on the graded pipe or drain above the ground, is wholly outside the junction area". In other words, the vertical projection of the stack must be kept wholly outside the junction area of the graded pipe or drain — i.e. not overlapping the junction at all (see Figure 6.8.3(b)). No dimensional offset is stated in the clause itself; the requirement is expressed as 'wholly outside the junction area'.

answers.answer: The minimum distance for connections to a stack above its base, for a stack extending more than five floor levels above the base, is 1 m, measured vertically from the base of the stack to the invert of the branch. This is the distance within which branches shall not connect — i.e., the stack must be clear of branch connections for at least 1 m above the base. Clause 6.8.2(b) states: "1 m for stacks that extend more than five floor levels above the base of the stack." Item (c) of the same clause applies a 2.5 m distance only "for all stacks in areas where foaming is likely to occur", which does not apply here since foaming is not likely. Clause 6.8.2(a) gives 600 mm for stacks not more than five floor levels. Note the question's framing of this as a required "length of the stack above the connection" should be read as the no-connection zone above the base: 1 m.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2021, Clause 8.5.7.5.5 ("Connection of all other fixtures") requires that fixtures other than basins and bidets connected to a group-vented branch "have a length of any DN 100 fixture discharge pipe not greater than 6 m" (8.5.7.5.5(b)). The maximum length of a DN 100 fixture discharge pipe is therefore 6 m. Note this is distinct from the 2.5 m limit that applies to fixture discharge pipes smaller than DN 100 (8.5.7.5.5(c)), and the basin/bidet DN 40 limit of 2.5 m in Clause 8.5.7.5.4.

answers.answer: The question describes a DN 100 stack of one floor with the top section graded, serving the first floor above ground level in a domestic or residential building (Clause 9.8.5 'DN 100 stack of one floor with top section graded'). The maximum stack loading permitted is 90 fixture units. Clause 9.8.5(b) states: 'The stack loading shall not exceed 90 fixture units.' This is consistent with the summary of variations in Clause 9.8.1(d) ('A DN 100 stack of one floor in height with top section graded (nominally horizontal), receiving a maximum discharge of 90 fixture units') and with Figure 9.8.5 ('Typical DN 100 stack with topmost section nominally horizontal for one floor — 90 fixture units'). Note the contrast with the multi-floor case: a DN 100 stack up to three floors with the top section graded is limited to 30 fixture units (Clause 9.8.4(b)). The edition used is AS/NZS 3500.2:2021, which the library marks edition_status: published; no superseded notice appears in the excerpts, though house rules note a 2025 edition was published on 2025-04-17, so a check against that edition is advisable.

Clause 9.9.3 states: 'Laundry troughs shall be connected only to the upper section of a DN 100 stack in accordance with Table 9.9.3.' The table row reads: '5 | 450 | 50' for maximum height 5, minimum distance 450 mm, and 50 fixture units. The library edition used is the published AS/NZS 3500.2:2021; note that the 2025 edition has since been published (2025-04-17), so this 2021 edition is superseded — check the 2025 edition if the current requirement is needed.

answers.answer: For a graded offset, where a water closet pan is the lowest fixture connected into the upper vertical section, the normal 900 mm restricted distance may be reduced to 600 mm, provided the WC pan's fixture discharge pipe is fitted with a DN 40 trap vent. Clause 9.9.6(c) states: "No connection shall be made to the vertical section within 900 mm of the upper offset bend. Where a water closet pan is the lowest fixture connected, the distance may be reduced to 600 mm, provided the fixture discharge pipe from the water closet pan is fitted with a DN 40 trap vent (see Figure 9.9.5)." Figure 9.9.5 (Graded offset) reflects the same 600 mm minimum for the vented-WC case. Edition used: AS/NZS 3500.2:2021 (published; this is the edition held in the library — note the 2025 edition was published 2025-04-17, so this 2021 edition is superseded; check the 2025 edition for the current requirement).

The same minimum 6 mm annular space applies where a branch discharge pipe traverses a floor or wall within 450 mm of its junction with a stack.

answers.answer: Clause 16.10.3(c) requires the vacuum lift pipe to rise a minimum of 80 mm above the soffit of the horizontal vacuum pipe it connects to. The full clause states the lift pipe shall (a) connect to the soffit of a horizontal vacuum pipe with a 45° junction in the direction of flow; (b) not be connected to a horizontal vacuum pipe in a location that holds water; (c) rise a minimum of 80 mm above soffit of the horizontal vacuum pipe it is connecting to; and (d) not be less than 150 mm between vacuum lift pipe connections on a common horizontal vacuum pipe.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2021 Clause 16.10.4(d), the second stage lift pipe must be installed with a vacuum reforming pocket when it is greater than 900 mm. The clause caps the second stage lift at a maximum of 2 m (item (c)); the 900 mm figure is the threshold above which a vacuum reforming pocket is required, not a 'minimum height'. A second stage lift of less than 900 mm does not require a vacuum reforming pocket (NOTE to 16.10.4, referring to Figure 16.10.4(B)). The question's phrasing ('minimum height at which a ... pocket must be installed') is slightly imprecise: the requirement is triggered when the lift exceeds 900 mm.
values: 900 mm (threshold above which a vacuum reforming pocket is required)

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2021 Clause 16.13.2, above-ground vacuum drainage pipes must have bilateral bracing within 500 mm each side of a change of direction or branch connection. The clause states: "For above-ground installation, vacuum drainage pipes shall be installed in accordance with Clauses 3.6, 10.2, 10.3, 10.4, 10.7, 10.8, 10.9, 10.10 and 10.13. In addition to Clause 16.13.1, vacuum drainage pipes shall have bilateral bracing within 500 mm each side of change of direction or branch connection, see Figure 16.13.2." Figure 16.13.2 (p.207) confirms the dimension: "Bilateral bracing to be within 500 mm of branch line connection or change of direction". Note that Clause 16.12(d) (p.205) also requires vacuum branch connections to be "braced bilaterally on each side of the 45° junction within 500 mm" — same figure (Figure 16.13.2) applies. Edition used: AS/NZS 3500.2:2021 (published, edition_status: published). Caveat per house rules: the 2025 edition of AS/NZS 3500.2 (published 2025-04-17) is one edition newer than the library copy; if the 2025 edition is available, verify whether this figure has changed.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2021, the vacuum test for a vacuum drainage system is governed by Clause 16.15. After the −55 ± 5 kPa test pressure has been reached, the pump is shut off, the vacuum is allowed to stabilize for a minimum of 3 min, and then the vacuum is allowed to fall to −50 kPa and the time recorded over the minimum test duration in Table 16.15.3. For DN 300 at a 250 m test length, Table 16.15.3 gives a minimum test duration of 23 min (acceptance time for a 1 kPa pressure change). The section must not show a drop in vacuum greater than −1 kPa over that minimum test duration (Clause 16.15.3). Note: the library does not set out the question's figure directly as a single "DN 300, 250 m = 23 min" statement — it must be read from Table 16.15.3 — but the table row for DN 225/300 gives 13 / 23 min for the 250 m column, i.e. 23 min for DN 300. Edition used: AS/NZS 3500.2:2021 (published edition held in the library).

answers.answer: The maximum permitted vacuum drop is 1 kPa over the minimum test duration. Clause 16.15.3 states: "The section of sanitary plumbing or sanitary drainage being tested shall not have a drop in vacuum greater than −1 kPa over the minimum test duration specified in Table 16.15.3." The test start described in your question (after stabilisation, allowing the vacuum to fall to −50 kPa and then recording time and vacuum drop) is the clause 16.15.2/16.15.3 procedure; the permitted drop is 1 kPa. Note that the minimum test duration is not a single value — it comes from Table 16.15.3 and depends on pipe size (DN) and test length (e.g. 2 min for DN 40–65 up to 300 m, up to 29 min for DN 300 at 300 m); the relevant cell must be read for the actual DN and length.

answers.answer: For an in-situ rectangular brickwork stormwater pit where the wall depth (measured from the existing surface to the invert of the outlet) is 500 mm, the minimum brickwork wall thickness is 110 mm. Clause 7.5.5.1(a)(i) sets brickwork wall thickness by depth: walls that do not exceed 600 mm must be 110 mm min. thick; walls exceeding 600 mm but not 1500 mm must be 230 mm min. thick. A 500 mm depth falls in the first band, so 110 mm applies. The pit must also be constructed in situ on a 150 mm min. thick concrete bed with at least the same external dimensions as the pit.
values: 110 mm min. thick (brickwork, wall depth ≤ 600 mm)

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2018, clause 5.4.4(c) requires any pipework that penetrates a concrete slab on ground to be at right angles to the slab surface and lagged for the full depth of the slab penetration with either (i) an impermeable flexible material of not less than 6 mm thickness, or (ii) an impermeable plastics sleeve or conduit providing equivalent protection. So the minimum thickness of impermeable flexible lagging is 6 mm, applied for the full depth of the slab penetration. Note: the 2018 edition held in the library is marked superseded (the 2021 edition repeats the same 6 mm requirement in its clause 5.5.4(c)).

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.1:2018, buried water services installed under slabs and footings (concrete) require a minimum cover of 75 mm, measured from the proposed finished surface levels. Clause 5.9 states: "Where water services are installed below ground, the minimum cover shall be as specified in Table 5.9, measured from the proposed finished surface levels." Table 5.9 (Minimum depth of cover for buried pipes) lists "Under slabs and footings (concrete) 75" mm. Note the library edition (2018) is marked superseded; the same 75 mm figure also appears in the 2015 edition held. This cover value should be read together with Clause 5.4.4(a), which requires a minimum 75 mm between the top of the pipe and the underside of the slab or slab-stiffening beam.

answers.answer: The standard does not set one single maximum length: it depends on the fixture. Under Clause 4.6.7.3 each fixture or fixture pair connected to a floor waste gully must have a separate waste pipe at a grade of not less than 2.5% "with a length not exceeding that specified in Table 4.6.7.2". In Table 4.6.7.2 the "Fixture untrapped" column (waste pipe connected to the riser of a floor waste gully) gives 1.2 m for most fixtures (bain-marie/sterilizer, bar sinks, bath, shower, bidet, cleaners' sink, clothes-washing machine, laundry and ablution trough, refrigerated cabinet). Basins and drinking fountains are "Not permitted" untrapped, and a tundish is allowed 10.0 m. Appendix B repeats 1.2 m for the untrapped DN 40/DN 50 fixture wastes it lists. Where an untrapped waste connects to a submerged inlet floor waste gully, Table 4.6.7.2 shows "Not allowed" for most fixtures. Note the edition: AS/NZS 3500.2:2018 is marked superseded in the library (edition_status: superseded).
values: 1.2 m (most fixtures, untrapped to FWG riser)

answers.answer: Clause 9.2.5 of AS/NZS 3500.2:2018 states: "Where the distance between the invert of the drain or graded pipe and the lowest floor level exceeds 2.4 m, that floor shall be counted as an additional floor level." So the lowest floor is counted as an extra floor level when the invert-to-lowest-floor distance exceeds 2.4 m. Figure 9.2.5 in the same clause illustrates this (annotated "If > 2.4 m (See Clause 9.2.5)"). Edition used: AS/NZS 3500.2:2018, which is marked superseded in the library (library's latest edition is 2018; be aware a later edition may exist — check the current edition).

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2018 Clause 9.9.5 (Graded offsets), a DN 100 stack provided with a graded offset between the base of the stack and the highest connection is limited to a height of 10 consecutive floor levels: "Only one graded offset shall be installed in any stack" and "The height of the stack shall not exceed 10 consecutive floor levels." So the maximum is 10 consecutive floor levels. Note also Clause 9.9.6(a): where fixtures are connected into the upper vertical section above the offset, that section above the upper offset bend shall not exceed five consecutive floor levels. The edition used (AS/NZS 3500.2:2018) is flagged in the library as superseded; the 2025 edition is the current one and should be checked.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2018, Clause 9.9.5 applies to DN 100 stacks offset between the base of the stack and the highest connection (graded offsets). A separate rule in 9.8.7.1(b) gives 1 m, but that applies to waste stacks (as a variation), not to this DN 100 single-stack graded-offset case.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2018 Clause 15.1, sanitary fixtures are tested by subjecting them to normal use, and after each test the residual water seal in the trap of the fixture concerned (or in any other trap connected to the same system) must, under normal operating conditions, retain a water seal of not less than 25 mm. answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.2:2018, Clause 15.2, sanitary drainage being hydrostatically tested shall be filled with water "to a height of not less than 1 m above the soffit level at the highest point of the section being tested" (Clause 15.2(a), p.177). The same clause also caps the head: the fill shall not exceed 3 m at the lowest point of the test section (Clause 15.2(c)), and the pressure is to be held without leakage for at least 15 min. Note that this 1 m figure applies to sanitary drainage; for sanitary plumbing the water level is taken to the spill level of the highest fixture or the flood level of the lowest sanitary fixture, whichever is higher (Clause 15.2(b)). Edition used: AS/NZS 3500.2:2018, which the library marks as superseded — check the current edition before relying on this figure.

answers.answer: Under AS/NZS 3500.3:2018, Clause 5.4.11.2 (the general design method for a pipe drain of a site stormwater drain), the full-pipe velocity shall not exceed 2.0 m/s — "The full-pipe velocity shall not exceed 2.0 m/s." A NOTE to that clause adds that, to reduce the possibility of overflow from stormwater pits due to increased energy losses, the full-pipe velocity in the outlet pipe should not exceed 1.5 m/s. Note this 1.5 m/s figure is guidance (a NOTE / "should"), while the 2.0 m/s limit is the mandatory requirement. answers.answer: For an underground OSD tank with open storage zones, the tank floors must be graded at a minimum slope of 1:140 towards the outlet, to minimise ponding and depositing of debris. answers.answer: The premise in the question is wrong: AS/NZS 3500.2:2021 Clause 3.6.7 does not require 300 mm. Clause 3.6.7 (Crossover of underground services) requires a vertical separation of not less than 100 mm where an underground drain crosses a service (or an underground service crosses a drain). The clause also requires crossing at an angle of not less than 45° and marker tape laid 150 mm above the installed service for 1 m either side of the centre-line. The library's 300 mm figures appear in other, unrelated provisions (Table 3.7.2 minimum cover of 300 mm for cast iron/ductile iron under vehicular traffic and for other materials in all other locations; and Clause 3.6.6 separation of 300 mm from a stormwater drain exceeding DN 100), not in Clause 3.6.7.
